thread:
maria: Quick q — need to confirm retention + deletion path for a customer request. They want all request logs + traces purged for org 'acme-inc' from Hosted. Who owns review/approval? :thinking:

owen: We have a standard flow: 1) confirm data scope 2) compliance sign-off 3) run deletion job + verify. For hosted customers, compliance + sec must sign off. Who's owning the scope check?

maria: I can pull the query slices. Mostly request logs (api_access logs), a few debug traces in jaeger with tag customer=acme-inc, and some short-term cache entries (prefix cache).

lee: @maria can you paste one example log id or query so we can identify indexes? also, are these within 90d retention or outside it?

maria: Example log id: 2025-11-09-api-req-8f3a. Most are within 120d window (so past default 90d). Customer claims legal obligation to delete older entries.

security-bot: FYI — deletion of logs beyond policy requires a documented retention exception and approval from @security and @compliance. See <https://intra.redwood/retention-policy#exceptions>. :information_source:

owen: OK — @maria please open an internal ticket in INFRA-RETENTION with: scope list, sample ids, export of matching trace IDs, and the customer's deletion confirmation. Tag it "retention-exception". We'll route to security/compliance for approval. :thumbsup:

maria: Filed INFRA-RETENTION-4123 with the details and attached CSV of 762 matching log ids. Link: <https://go/infra/INFRA-RETENTION-4123>

lee: For the actual purge, use retentionctl (it runs an audited job + creates a signed deletion report). Example command we use in staging:
```
# run dry-run first
retentionctl purge --service api-logs --selector "customer:acme-inc" --dry-run \
  --since 1970-01-01 --report /tmp/acme-delete-report.json

# actual run (once approved)
retentionctl purge --service api-logs --selector "customer:acme-inc" \
  --since 1970-01-01 --report /secure/reports/acme-delete-report.json --auth-tier sec-approved
```

maria: Great. Does retentionctl cover jaeger traces and prefix caches too?

sre-oncall: retentionctl currently supports logs (ES/Clickhouse) and traces (jaeger via trace-indexer). For in-memory prefix caches (redis) we need a separate flush job — scope it in the ticket. I can add a runbook step: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "cache:prefix:acme-inc:*" | xargs -r redis-cli del` (with caution).

security-bot: Reminder: before running deletion, ensure legal has sent signed request (pdf) and we record the deletion hash in the ticket. Audit record must include operator, command, report SHA256.

maria: Copy. I'll attach legal's request and mark the ticket blocked-by: security/compliance.

owen: Once sec approves, ping me here and I'll coordinate a low-traffic window to run (avoid 12:00-14:00 PST). Also plan a quick verification query and store report in the compliance bucket. :eyes:

lee: After deletion, we should run a sampling check for 7 days to ensure no stragglers show up in derived datasets (analytics pipelines). Add that to the ticket as post-delete verification.

maria: Updated INFRA-RETENTION-4123 with those steps. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

sre-oncall: If anyone needs me to run the redis flush, ping me directly. I'll coordinate with oncall to avoid impact.
